titre: Rumored The Simpsons: Hit & Run remake may be in trouble after one developer says their "mind-blowingly awesome" project is cancelled
chapo: A rumored remake of The Simpsons: Hit & Run (the internet's most-wanted video game revival) may be in trouble. Read more
extrait: A rumored remake of The Simpsons: Hit & Run (the internet's most-wanted video game revival) may be in trouble. Just earlier this year, Radical Entertainment made somewhat of a comeback as New Radical Games - with the original studio's co-founder (Ian Wilkinson) and former developer (Tim Bennison) serving as New Radical's CEO and COO, respectively. The company best known for Prototype and the well-remembered open-world Simpsons game was back, in some sense. Whatever project the studio was cooking hasn't been so lucky, it seems. New Radical Games senior game designer Darren Evenson recently said an upcoming project at the company had been scrapped, and he's now looking for new work, per a LinkedIn post. "It seems that not even a fantastic project with an absolutely incredible team is immune from the current state of the industry right now, as what we were working on at New Radical Games (although mind-blowingly awesome) was part of a whole gaggle of cancellations," Evenson wrote. "A gaggle, I say!" "Oh, you silly suits with spreadsheets... will you EVER learn? If you don't make the game, you can't make the money... and if you don't make the money, then you don't get the power... and... well, there's more to that quote, but I digress." "For the first time in my career, I am Available For Work and looking for a new exciting opportunity where I can make some fun games with some great people," he added. "Please reach out, shout out, or perform some interpretive dance if you know of an opportunity that a hip cat like me could groove to." New Radical Games has never formally revealed its plans, but a couple clues pointed to something Simpsons-shaped. As VGC noted, Evenson's statement echoes a few popular lines from the iconic animated sitcom. "Will you ever learn" is suspiciously close to a particular Troy McClure quote, for one. Then there's seemingly a Scarface riff in the developer's statement - one that was also parodied in The Simpsons, of course: "In America, first you get the sugar, then you get the power, then you get the women." It's worth noting Radical Entertainment did also make Scarface: The World Is Yours, so this one could go either way. But the most eyebrow-raising clue came from original Simpsons co-showrunner and creator Matt Groening. During a Disney D23 panel this summer, Groening and current showrunner Matt Selman were asked about the possibility of a Hit & Run comeback. titre: The Simpsons Hit & Run remake may have been cancelled as developer seemingly hints they were working on it
chapo: Speculation surrounding a remake has been rife since Matt Groening suggested it was coming
extrait: Speculation surrounding a remake has been rife since Matt Groening suggested it was coming The remake of The Simpsons: Hit & Run that was rumoured to be in development may now have been cancelled. There’s been some speculation that a remake was in the works, particularly when its studio Radical Entertainment returned this year as New Radical Games and included Hit & Run artwork on its homepage that was slightly different to that of the original game. This was then followed by apparent confirmation by Simpsons creator Matt Groening, who seemingly let slip during the D23 conference in August that the original game was returning. Now it appears that we may never see a remake after all, with New Radical Games senior game designer Darren Evenson posting on LinkedIn that the studio’s unannounced project had been scrapped and he was now looking for work as a result. “It seems that not even a fantastic project with an absolutely incredible team is immune from the current state of the industry right now, as what we were working on at New Radical Games (although mind-blowingly awesome) was part of a whole gaggle of cancellations,” he wrote. “A gaggle, I say! “Oh, you silly suits with spreadsheets… will you EVER learn? If you don’t make the game, you can’t make the money… and if you don’t make the money, then you don’t get the power… and… well, there’s more to that quote, but I digress. “For the first time in my career, I am Available For Work and looking for a new exciting opportunity where I can make some fun games with some great people! Please reach out, shout out, or perform some interpretive dance if you know of an opportunity that a hip cat like me could groove to.” While Evenson doesn’t explicitly say that he’s referring to The Simpsons Hit & Run, the “will you ever learn” echoes a popular Troy McClure line from the show (“oh, Shakazaramesh, will you ever learn?”). His line about “if you don’t make the money, then you don’t get the power” could refer to the movie Scarface, where Tony Montana says: “In this country, you gotta make the money first. Then when you get the money, you get the power. Then when you get the power, then you get the women.” Radical Entertainment also developed Scarface: The World is Yours, which means Evenson may have been referring to a Scarface game instead.
